newsitem.title: USA: Kiwi postpones press conference on service resumption.
newsitem.headline: Kiwi postpones press conference on service resumption.

text.p: Bankrupt discount carrier Kiwi International Air Lines, which was expected to outline its return to service Thursday, postponed a press conference until Nov. 4.
The airline did not comment on the reason for the delay.
Kiwi, however, said it will still present a financing plan Thursday that would enable it to rehire laid-off employees and restart operations.
Kiwi said it expected the U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Newark, N.J., to approve a $5 million debtor-in-possession financing commitment from the Wasatch Group.
Kiwi and Wasatch signed a definitive agreement on the financing pact on Wednesday.
Kiwi filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Sept. 30, 1996 under a $40 million debt load and suspended flights on Oct. 15. Its 15-jet fleet remains inactive.
